newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl, Simitis say EMU rules must be fairly applied.
newsitem.headline: Kohl, Simitis say EMU rules must be fairly applied.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Greek prime minister Costas Simitis agreed on Thursday that the criteria for European monetary union (EMU) should apply equally to all prospective participants, Simitis told reporters.
Two hours of talks between the two leaders covered a range of topics including EMU.
"We discussed the European economic and monetary union. We were of the view that it should be avoided that different countries should be treated differently," Simitis said.
"The same criteria, whatever they may be, should be applied to all states in equal measure," he said.
On the pending reform of European Union institutions, Simitis said it was important that smaller countries have a say in decisions.
The intergovernmental conference discussing the reforms should be completed by midyear.
A European Commission report issued on Wednesday said that Greece and Italy were the only two of the 15 EU member states that would not fulfil the fiscal criteria for currency union.
The report forecast Greece's public sector deficit at 4.9 percent of gross domestic product this year, falling to 3.4 percent next year.
Its outstanding debt was seen at 108.3 percent of GDP, falling to 104.9 percent next year.

The Maastricht Treaty includes "reference values" that countries participating in EMU should reduce their deficits to three percent of GDP and debt to 60 percent of GDP. But it allows leeway to include states whose values exceed those levels if they are making steady progress toward the goals.
